Athaliah
ath-a-LYE-uh
proper noun (figure)
Hebrew Athalyah (H6271) — possibly "Yahweh is exalted" or "Yahweh has constrained"; uncertain. The Yahwistic ending is striking on a queen who actively worked to extinguish Yahwistic worship in Judah; ancient Near Eastern theophoric names often outlived the religious commitments they originally signaled.

📖 Biblical Definition

Athaliah (c. 841 — 835 BC) was the only queen regnant in the history of the divided southern kingdom of Judah (2 Kings 11; 2 Chronicles 22:10-23:21), daughter of Omri and Ahab of Israel and granddaughter of Jezebel, who married Jehoram king of Judah (the son of the faithful Jehoshaphat) and brought the Omride apostasy with her into the Davidic house. When her husband Jehoram died and her son Ahaziah of Judah was killed by Jehu's revolt in Israel (2 Kings 9:27), Athaliah seized power in Jerusalem by murdering every member of the Davidic royal family she could find — her own grandsons — in a comprehensive dynastic massacre intended to extinguish the line of David and replace it with the Omride dynasty extending into Judah. Only the infant Joash escaped, hidden by his aunt Jehosheba (the wife of the high priest Jehoiada) for six years in the temple while Athaliah reigned as queen. The episode is one of the most extraordinary in Scripture: the Davidic covenant of 2 Samuel 7:16 ("thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever") came perilously close to extinction through a single hand, the hand of Jezebel's daughter. In the seventh year of Athaliah's reign (835 BC) Jehoiada the high priest organized a coordinated coup: the Levitical guard formed a protective ring around the boy-king Joash, the elders crowned him in the temple, the people of Judah shouted "God save the king," and Athaliah was led out from the temple precinct (so as not to defile it with her blood) and killed at the horse-gate of the palace. Her seven-year usurpation is the only break in the unbroken Davidic line from David to Zedekiah, and the Davidic covenant survived only by the courage of the high priest's wife and the providence of the LORD over the one infant who escaped.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Only queen regnant of Judah (c. 841-835 BC); daughter of Ahab and Jezebel of Israel; married Jehoram of Judah; murdered her own Davidic grandsons to seize the throne; reigned 7 years; deposed by the high priest Jehoiada's coup that installed the boy-king Joash; killed at the horse-gate.

ATHALIAH, proper noun. Hebrew Athalyah (H6271); uncertain meaning; possibly "Yahweh is exalted" or "Yahweh has constrained."

Daughter of Ahab and Jezebel of Israel (or, by some readings, of Omri); married Jehoram king of Judah, son of the faithful Jehoshaphat.

After her son Ahaziah of Judah was killed in Jehu's revolt (2 Kings 9:27), she murdered every Davidic royal she could find and reigned as queen regnant of Judah for 7 years (c. 841-835 BC).

Only the infant Joash escaped, hidden in the temple by his aunt Jehosheba (wife of the high priest Jehoiada).

Deposed by Jehoiada's coordinated coup at the temple; killed at the horse-gate of the palace (2 Kings 11:16).

📖 Key Scripture

2 Kings 11:1-3 — "And when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal. But Jehosheba, the daughter of king Joram, sister of Ahaziah, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons which were slain; and they hid him, even him and his nurse, in the bedchamber from Athaliah, so that he was not slain. And he was with her hid in the house of the LORD six years. And Athaliah did reign over the land."

2 Samuel 7:16 — "And thine house and thy kingdom shall be established for ever before thee: thy throne shall be established for ever."

2 Chronicles 22:10-11 — "But when Athaliah the mother of Ahaziah saw that her son was dead, she arose and destroyed all the seed royal of the house of Judah. But Jehoshabeath, the daughter of the king, took Joash the son of Ahaziah, and stole him from among the king's sons that were slain, and put him and his nurse in a bedchamber. So Jehoshabeath, the daughter of king Jehoram, the wife of Jehoiada the priest..."

Psalm 89:33-37 — "Nevertheless my lovingkindness will I not utterly take from him, nor suffer my faithfulness to fail. My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips. Once have I sworn by my holiness that I will not lie unto David. His seed shall endure for ever, and his throne as the sun before me."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Athaliah is corrupted when her queenship is read through modern feminist lenses as merely a queen who happened to be evil rather than as the deliberate Omride-dynastic invasion of the Davidic line, when her seven-year reign is treated as a curiosity rather than as the moment the Davidic covenant nearly failed, or when Jehosheba's quiet heroism is overlooked beside the more dramatic Jehoiada-coup.

expand to see more

Female-monarch-as-modern-cause. Some contemporary readings present Athaliah as an early example of female political agency — a woman who took power, ruled, and was killed. The text refuses this framing. The chapters resist any sympathetic reading of Athaliah: she is depicted as the granddaughter of Jezebel completing what her grandmother began, murdering her own Davidic grandsons to extinguish the line of David, and ruling Judah on Omride-pagan principles while the rightful king hid in the temple. The text's interest is not in her gender but in her covenant-treason against the Davidic dynasty her mother-in-law had been brought into to corrupt.

Jehosheba-overlooked. Jehoiada the high priest gets named more often in the narrative, but the woman who actually preserved the Davidic line was Jehosheba (also spelled Jehoshabeath), Jehoram's daughter and Joash's aunt and Jehoiada's wife. While Athaliah was systematically killing the royal children, Jehosheba slipped the infant Joash out of the slaughter and hid him with his nurse in the temple bedchamber for six years. The Davidic covenant survived through a high-priest's wife who refused to let the line of David die. The text honors her by naming her in both 2 Kings 11:2 and 2 Chr 22:11.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew Athalyah (H6271); uncertain meaning, possibly "Yahweh is exalted." The only queen regnant of Judah (c. 841-835 BC); daughter of Ahab and Jezebel; usurped after Davidic massacre; deposed by Jehoiada.

Married Jehoram king of Judah, son of the faithful Jehoshaphat; mother of Ahaziah of Judah

Usage

"Athaliah — the only queen regnant of Judah; daughter of Ahab and Jezebel; nearly extinguished the Davidic line."

"Hidden in the house of the LORD six years — the seven-year suspension of the Davidic line, broken by the courage of Jehosheba."
